note: v1 91.54 (seeds 0/11 91.54/91.54): CALL AND RETURN - first draft of an ELECTRO FUGUE MACHINE. An eight-bar subject over a four-bar loop (i - VI - iv - V), written so it canons against itself four bars later, is taken up in turn by an FM bell (phase modulation 3.5:1), a hard-synced lead, a PWM wavetable pulse and an FM bass over a motorik machine kit; then the machine starts CALLING: a seeded grammar pushes and pops a call stack every four bars, and each level spawns a faster copy of the current bar an octave higher (sixteenths, thirty-seconds, then sixty-fourths blurring into a glass shimmer) - the texture's density and level follow the stack; each calls section RETURNS (the stack empties, the drums pull back to a kick and a rim fill). The canon modulates - D minor, G minor (an electro-break kick, the pulse arpeggiating, the sync lead resting), A minor (half time, the voices crossed) - all tuned in WERCKMEISTER III, a well temperament, so each key has its own colour; then a return (the subject alone, augmented, on the bell), a final call that fills the stack to the top and unwinds, and an outro of bell tolls. 152 bars at 120 bpm, 5:04. Weakest term: rhythm (the quantised machine has no off-grid share; I will humanize it next). Not heard by me.

v2 92.24 (seed 0; v1 re-scored 91.70): THE MACHINE'S CLAVE. Call and Return was a perfectly square machine - every onset on the eighth-note grid (compscore: off-grid share 0.00, rhythm 56). Now, through the calls, the FM bass plays three-three-two sixteenths twice a bar - a tresillo, root, root, octave / root, fifth, octave - and the open hat follows it instead of the off-beat, while the kick stays four on the floor and the canon runs straight above: the groove leans across the beat under a fugue that does not. Rhythm 56 -> 65, structure 97, the joins a little closer (flow 55). Also tried the clave in the kick for the first calls: no further gain, and the floor is better kept. Not heard by me.
